summary: US equities posted modest gains Tuesday as investors positioned ahead of Nvidia's critical earnings report due Wednesday and awaited fresh inflation data. The S&P 500 climbed 0.32% to 7,677 while the Nasdaq advanced 0.66% to 26,151, led by a semiconductor rebound after Monday's selloff. Oil prices extended their decline, with crude falling toward $80, providing relief to inflation concerns. Markets are also focused on new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech later this week and key PCE inflation data due Wednesday morning alongside revised Q2 GDP figures. Meanwhile, US-Canada trade tensions escalated as Canada announced retaliatory tariffs in response to Trump administration duties, though both nations have kept oil off the negotiation table for now. Bitcoin rallied above $79,000, extending a 23% weekly gain, while Treasury yields retreated from recent highs following reports of expanded debt buyback operations.

signals.title: Nvidia earnings create index-level volatility risk
signals.desc: Nvidia reports Wednesday after the close with markets hyper-focused on data-center demand, margins and fiscal Q3 outlook as the AI bellwether faces extreme positioning after a recent losing streak.

signals.title: PCE inflation gauge and revised GDP data on deck
signals.desc: July PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, arrives Wednesday morning alongside Q2 GDP revisions and durable goods orders, creating a macro data cluster that could swing Treasury yields.

signals.title: Bitcoin extends rally on 23% weekly surge
signals.desc: Bitcoin climbed above $79,000 as Treasury debt buyback news pushed yields lower and crypto market sentiment improved, with Bitcoin dominance rising to 58% amid broad-based digital asset gains.

signals.title: US-Canada trade war escalates with retaliatory tariffs
signals.desc: Canada announced new retaliatory tariffs responding to Trump administration's 50% duties on steel, dairy and other goods, though both nations have kept oil off the table, limiting immediate commodity impact.

signals.title: Oil decline eases inflation pressure before PCE print
signals.desc: WTI crude extended losses toward $80 per barrel on weak demand signals and inventory builds, reducing headline inflation risk ahead of Wednesday's PCE data and supporting equity multiples.

verdict: Markets face a critical inflection point Wednesday with Nvidia earnings and PCE data likely to dictate near-term direction amid elevated positioning and cross-currents from falling oil, rising trade tensions, and Fed transition uncertainty.
